claims.text: Graph neural networks can accurately predict melting temperatures across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Graph neural networks can accurately predict enthalpies of fusion across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Graph neural networks can accurately predict entropies of fusion across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Graph neural networks can accurately predict volume changes at melting across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Graph neural networks can accurately predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The proposed intervention is to train a graph neural network on high-entropy alloys with known thermodynamic properties.
Configurational entropy of mixing mediates the thermodynamic properties targeted by the model.
Enthalpies of mixing of the constituent elements mediate the thermodynamic properties targeted by the model.
Graph neural-network regression can learn complex relationships between alloy composition and thermodynamic properties.
The proposed model will improve prediction accuracy relative to CALPHAD and experimental measurements.
The proposed model will improve efficiency relative to CALPHAD and experimental measurements.
CALPHAD and experimental measurements are current approaches for assessing high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic and thermal behavior.
The approach is limited to compositions and property ranges represented in the training dataset.
Predictions for compositions or properties outside the training dataset have uncertain accuracy.
Performance will be evaluated on a separate test dataset using MAE and R-squared.
The hypothesis is to be rejected if MAE exceeds 10% or R-squared is below 0.8.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims applicability across the high-entropy-alloy family, while the boundary limits applicability to compositions and properties within the training dataset and the uncertainty field concedes unreliable extrapolation outside it.
